purpose: Secondary-market and legacy accelerators whose memory capacity, bandwidth, software lifecycle, or used pricing can make them relevant to local LLM inference.
notes: Used-market prices are point-in-time observations and must be compared with shipping, taxes, import fees, seller reputation, cooling requirements and software lifecycle.
A low purchase price does not imply low total cost: passive datacenter cards often require server-class forced airflow and may need older software stacks.
Legacy CUDA and ROCm compatibility is treated as a first-class constraint rather than assuming current frameworks support every older accelerator.

software: llama.cpp CUDA builds compiled for Pascal
older PyTorch/CUDA combinations where Pascal binaries remain available
hardware.software_lifecycle_warning: CUDA Toolkit 13.x removed offline compilation and library support for Pascal. CUDA 12.x remains the practical native build ceiling, so modern framework support must be verified before purchase.
hardware.model_size_practicality: 16GB HBM2 is useful for smaller and mid-sized quantized models, but capacity is the main limitation. The 732 GB/s memory bandwidth is unusually high at current used prices and can make the card interesting for models that fit entirely in VRAM.
quantization_compatibility: no Tensor Cores; modern tensor-core-specific low-bit acceleration paths are unavailable
hardware.off_grid_suitability: low; 250W board power plus required forced airflow outweighs the strong bandwidth-per-dollar for solar-constrained systems.
hardware.performance_per_watt_status: poor by current standards; value proposition is purchase price and HBM2 bandwidth, not energy efficiency

pricing.note: Canada-located used 16GB P100 listing observed at CA$200; other visible listings ranged lower before shipping/import costs.

interconnect: 92 GB/s peak Infinity Fabric link bandwidth
hardware.software_lifecycle_warning: Unlike MI50/gfx906, MI100 remains present in current ROCm compatibility/install documentation as an Instinct compute target. Exact OS, framework and ROCm release combinations still need verification.
hardware.model_size_practicality: 32GB HBM2 can hold many 30B-class quantized models depending on context and runtime overhead. The roughly 1.2 TB/s bandwidth is exceptional, but current used pricing is high enough that newer 32GB workstation GPUs may offer a better overall ownership experience.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: low; 300W board power and passive cooling requirements make it a poor fit for constrained solar systems despite excellent memory bandwidth.
hardware.performance_per_watt_status: legacy datacenter class; bandwidth is strong but power draw is high

pricing.note: Used MI100 listing at US$999, approximately CA$1,407.29 when observed; cross-border shipping/import charges can materially increase delivered cost.

hardware.form_factor: 4.4 in H x 10.5 in L, dual slot
hardware.model_size_practicality: 48GB ECC VRAM is highly useful for larger quantized models and multi-card inference, but the current Canadian used-market asking prices observed in this pass make it poor value compared with newer workstation and unified-memory alternatives.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: low; 300W passive datacenter card requiring strong chassis airflow.

pricing.note: Lowest clearly identified Canada-located A40 48GB listing visible in the observed search results was CA$6,250; many imported listings were higher. This is recorded as a market warning rather than a buying recommendation.
